The post YTL AI Labs Launches Cikgu ILMU To Support Children’s Learning appeared first on Lowyat.NET.
item.content:encoded:
YTL AI Labs previously launched ILMUchat, the AI assistant made using the ILMU LLM. Today, the company launched another AI-powered tool based on the same underlying LLM. It’s called Cikgu ILMU, and depending on perspective, it’s both a self-explanatory name, as well as a counterintuitive one at the same time.

Rather than teachers, Cikgu ILMU was built with parents in mind, according to the announcement. It is meant to make it simple for parents to get the help they need as they follow their children through their educational journey. The added benefit is that the guidance provided is grounded in the Malaysian national curriculum (KSSR and KSSM), to match what the children learn at school. All of this is stacked on top of ILMU itself already setting itself apart with local contextual familiarity, plus Bahasa Melayu understanding.

As the press release mentions, “parents may not always remember a subject, understand a homework question, or know how to help their children prepare for exams. With Cikgu ILMU, help can be as simple as taking a photograph of a homework question. AI can read the content and explain the concepts step by step, helping parents guide their children with confidence”.

More specifically, Cikgu ILMU provides four tools, the first of which is the Homework Help described above. Then there are Study Guides that help prepare guides for any subject that can be printed for offline use, containing not only key concepts and explanations but also diagrams and practice questions. On a related note, Quick Quiz generates questions and marks answers, as well as helping to identify learning gaps to be supplemented. Finally, there’s Flashcards, which is pretty self-explanatory.

Finally, beyond just English and Bahasa Melayu, Cikgu ILMU also supports Chinese and Tamil to help overcome any language barriers that may be present in the local context. YTL says that Cikgu ILMU is available for free on both the Apple App Store and Google Play Store alongside ILMUchat. It’s mostly the same story with its web client, but like ILMUchat, you have to first create an account to use it.

The post Fujifilm Launches Instax Mini Evo 2, Square 2 In Malaysia appeared first on Lowyat.NET.
item.content:encoded:
Fujifilm Malaysia has officially introduced two new instant cameras, the Instax mini Evo 2 and Instax Square 2. Both models are designed to offer different approaches to instant photography, with the former combining digital and analogue features while the latter sticks to a more traditional instant camera experience.

Instax Mini Evo 2

The Instax mini Evo 2 is a hybrid instant camera featuring a 4.5-inch touchscreen, which is the first of its kind among Instax devices. The display allows users to compose shots, adjust settings and preview images before printing them.

It also comes with Instax Expanded View, which provides a wider perspective and an on-screen framing guide. Meanwhile, its Instax Immersive Movie feature records the four seconds leading up to each shot, allowing users to preserve some of the moments preceding the actual capture.

For creative options, the camera offers 10 lens effects and 10 film effects, providing up to 100 possible combinations. These include four new shooting effects called Afterimage, Soft Focus, Yellow Green and Deep.

Instax Square 2

Meanwhile, the Instax Square 2 is an analogue instant camera that captures photos in a 1:1 square format. It features automatic exposure adjustment, which controls shutter speed and flash output to achieve optimal brightness, alongside a built-in selfie mirror.

The camera offers three shooting modes, namely Standard, Close-up and Landscape. The latter is a new addition intended for capturing distant subjects and group shots, while Close-up mode is suited for selfies and other nearby subjects.

Users can also apply one of two built-in mood filters, with Warm offering softer, warmer tones and Cool producing a crisper appearance. Alongside the camera, Fujifilm is also introducing its new Instax Soft Haze square-format film, which uses a newly developed emulsion to produce soft lighting effects and warmer colours.

Pricing And Availability

The Instax mini Evo 2 is available in Malaysia with a retail price of RM1,148, which includes a bundle with one pack of film. Fujifilm is also running a limited-time promotion where early buyers are entitled to receive an Infinity Kit and an exclusive Instax camera strap along with their purchase, though only while stocks last. 

Meanwhile, the Instax Square 2 has been available locally since 4 November 2026. It retails for RM508 as part of the Good Vibes Kit, which comes with a complimentary camera case during its early-bird promotion, while the new Soft Haze film is priced at RM58.

item.dc:creator: Nurul Kamil
item.description:
iQOO is gearing up to release some new products in Malaysia, namely the next generation of its flagship gaming smartphones. The iQOO 16 and iQOO 16s now have a confirmed launch date, and it’s not far ahead. The vivo sub-brand has announced that the upcoming smartphones will be debuting on 8 December 2026, which is […]

The post iQOO 16 Series Officially Launching Locally On 8 December appeared first on Lowyat.NET.
item.content:encoded:
iQOO is gearing up to release some new products in Malaysia, namely the next generation of its flagship gaming smartphones. The iQOO 16 and iQOO 16s now have a confirmed launch date, and it’s not far ahead.

The vivo sub-brand has announced that the upcoming smartphones will be debuting on 8 December 2026, which is a little under two weeks from now. Aside from confirming the launch date, the company has revealed a few details on the devices.

For starters, the iQOO 16 will feature a Samsung M16 2K 165Hz Display with 10,000 nits of local peak brightness. This is very likely the same 6.85-inch AMOLED panel equipped on its Chinese counterpart, which launched a few months prior. In any case, the version heading our way will also come with a Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 SoC and iQOO’s in-house Q4 gaming chip.

Although the company has not offered further details on the phone, we can expect it to come with a triple 50MP camera setup on the rear and a 32MP selfie snapper. Based on the Chinese model, it may also come with an 8,400mAh battery with 100W charging.

As for the 16s, the company revealed that it will sport a 6.59-inch 1.5K AMOLED screen with a 144Hz refresh rate and a peak brightness of 5,000 nits. Other than that, the phone will be equipped with a Snapdragon 8s Gen 4 SoC and a 7,650mAh battery. Beyond that, though, no other details on the device have been revealed thus far.

Ahead of the launch, the company has opened pre-bookings for the devices, allowing customers to reserve a unit ahead of time. Those interested have until 7 December 2026 to do so, and they must pay RM1. In exchange, they will be entitled to some early bird benefits, including an RM50 Petronas Petrol Card and a RM200 member discount. Bear in mind that this does not count as a phone purchase, as the full pricing for either device has yet to be revealed.

As per the pre-booking listings, both models will come in two finishes. For the iQOO 16, the options are Matrix and Alpha, while the 16s will be offered in Vector Grey and Shadow Black.

(Source: iQOO press release)

item.title: Harman Kardon Launches Allure 2, Liora Speakers
item.dc:creator: Ian Chee
item.description:
Audio brand Harman Kardon announced two new speakers today, both of which will be available by the end of the first week of December. These are the Allure 2 and Liora. While both can also serve as a source of ambient light, the former is by far the more conventional one of the two. Harman […]

The post Harman Kardon Launches Allure 2, Liora Speakers appeared first on Lowyat.NET.
item.content:encoded:
Audio brand Harman Kardon announced two new speakers today, both of which will be available by the end of the first week of December. These are the Allure 2 and Liora. While both can also serve as a source of ambient light, the former is by far the more conventional one of the two.

Harman Kardon Allure 2

With that in mind, let’s start with the Harman Kardon Allure 2, which looks very similar to many other products by the company. On the surface, this provides both 360 degrees of sound, as well as 360 degrees of ambient light. This makes it quite similar to the Aura Studio 5 that launched almost exactly a year ago.

Going into the details, the Harman Kardon Allure 2 features three 1.5-inch speakers and a 3.5-inch down-firing woofer that contribute to the 360-degree audio. Connectivity is enabled by Bluetooth 5.4, which allows simultaneous connection to two smart devices, as well as Auracast for multi-speaker setups.

On that note, controls for the speaker’s lighting and equaliser are managed via the Harman Kardon One app. Speaking of which, the Allure 2 has five LumiGlow lighting themes, with very self-explanatory names – Sunrise, Fireplace, Ocean, Aurora, and Blossom. Tweaks to these defaults are possible via the aforementioned mobile app as well. Turning this on is done with a single press of the light button on the speaker itself. With a double tap, this cycles the lighting to the next theme.

The Harman Kardon Allure 2 comes with a price tag of RM1,099. As mentioned earlier, availability starts on 7 December, via the brand’s official stores on Shopee and Lazada. Pre-order it before then, and you’ll get a complimentary aromatic candle worth RM99 thrown in.

Harman Kardon Liora

Moving on, the Harman Kardon Liora only does 180-degree sound rather than the full 360. That being said, it has a three-way speaker design, with two 5-inch subwoofers, four 2.5-inch mid-range speakers, and three 30mm tweeters. WiFi is also added in as an additional input option, and while this only runs Bluetooth 5.3, you still get Auracast support, as well as AirPlay 2 and Google Cast.

Fine-tuning is once again done with the Harman Kardon One app. Lighting options include the five that are available for the Allure 2, as well as five additional ones. These are Nebula, Calm, Starry, Bubble, and Coral, with the last three noted to be exclusive to the Liora.

One more element that the Liora has but the Allure 2 does not is what Harman Kardon calls the Moment button. Pressing this plays a predetermined playlist, album or soundscape. As you’d expect, this is changed via the One app. Finally, there is also the option to get a dedicated stand for the Liora.

The Harman Kardon Liora costs RM5,399 on its own, while the stand is priced at RM799, once again from either Shopee or Lazada. Get them within the pre-order period – which ends on 6 December – and you can get both bundled in for RM5,688 instead, as well as a Bespoke Fragrance Collection containing a room mist and an aromatic candle, worth RM299.

The post Harman Kardon Launches Allure 2, Liora Speakers appeared first on Lowyat.NET.

item.dc:creator: Nurul Kamil
item.description:

Well, the brand has decided that it’s about time for a name reveal. This device will henceforth be known […]

The post Mysterious Nothing AI Device Confirmed To Be Wireless Earbuds Called The Ear (note) appeared first on Lowyat.NET.
item.content:encoded:
By now, you’ve probably heard of Nothing’s upcoming mystery product, which the company founder and CEO Carl Pei characterised as a screenless device that will serve as a stepping stone for AI gadgets of the future. Well, the brand has decided that it’s about time for a name reveal. This device will henceforth be known as the Ear (note), and if the name isn’t enough of a giveaway, it will be a pair of earbuds.

Pei offered Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman a first look at the product, confirming some of its functions and capabilities. As expected, a major feature is recording, and Nothing is equipping both the charging case and the buds with microphones. According to the publication, the case can be used to record in-person meetings or classes. Meanwhile, the buds will be able to record calls. Transcription will also be available.

Furthermore, the case will come with a “Talk” button, much like the Ear (3). That said, this button will serve a different purpose. Apparently, pressing it will start recording, though the company is planning to introduce other functions as well. Meanwhile, a dedicated app will allow users to manage recordings, summaries, and transcriptions. Additionally, the buds will include a basic voice control system, as well as support for AI agents. Nothing also asserted that additional measures are in place to address privacy concerns.

For now, the company is still keeping much about the Ear (note) under wraps, including the design of the earbuds themselves, as well as specifications and pricing. These details will undoubtedly be revealed during the official launch on 8 December 2026.

In the meantime, the company will likely continue to build hype around the device with more teasers, though it’s hard to say if these buds have anything else going on for them. It seems that Nothing wants to present them as something different, but not the game-changing “iPhone of AI”.

So far though, the Ear (note) is leaning more on mundane. Earbuds aren’t a novel invention, and the brand already has a few under its belt. AI-based recording features are also a staple in many modern smartphones and other electronics. But time will tell if the upcoming buds have anything unique to offer.

(Source: Bloomberg via GSMArena)

The post Mysterious Nothing AI Device Confirmed To Be Wireless Earbuds Called The Ear (note) appeared first on Lowyat.NET.

item.dc:creator: Heirul Kamel
item.description:
Huawei has introduced the MateBook Fold S in China, which is a more compact take on its foldable laptop concept. While it still has a relatively large footprint, the device is essentially a smaller version of last year’s MateBook Fold, with a 14.7-inch foldable OLED display instead of the original’s 18-inch panel. One of its […]

The post Huawei Launches MateBook Fold S Foldable Laptop In China appeared first on Lowyat.NET.
item.content:encoded:
Huawei has introduced the MateBook Fold S in China, which is a more compact take on its foldable laptop concept. While it still has a relatively large footprint, the device is essentially a smaller version of last year’s MateBook Fold, with a 14.7-inch foldable OLED display instead of the original’s 18-inch panel.

One of its more interesting additions is a secondary display on the back, which Huawei calls the Live Square Screen. Resembling the cover screens found on flip-style foldable smartphones, it allows users to interact with certain features without having to unfold the main display.

The smaller screen can show notifications, calendar appointments and weather information. It also supports interaction with selected apps, while Huawei has demonstrated using it to start meeting recordings and generate meeting summaries through its AI assistant.

Like its larger sibling, the MateBook Fold S can be used in several configurations. Users can fold its main display halfway for a laptop-like experience with an on-screen keyboard, or unfold it completely to use as a tablet. It also comes with a built-in kickstand and supports Huawei’s M-Pencil stylus.

The MateBook Fold S has a 14.7-inch foldable OLED display with a 3:2 aspect ratio and 3,240 x 2,160 resolution. When folded, each half measures 10.2 inches diagonally, while the secondary display on the back measures 3.5 inches. Despite its relatively large screen, the device weighs just 639g, or 647g for the Cloud Sea Blue variant, excluding the keyboard.

Other specifications include a Kirin XE90 processor, up to 32GB of RAM and 1TB of storage. It also has a 46Wh battery, Wi-Fi 7 connectivity, Bluetooth 6.0 and two USB-C ports. The device runs HarmonyOS and is available in three colour options: Phantom Night Black, Sky White and Cloud Sea Blue.

In China, the MateBook Fold S starts at CNY14,999 (~RM9,299) for the 16GB RAM + 256GB storage configuration. The 16GB RAM + 512GB variant costs CNY16,999 (~RM10,539), while the 24GB RAM + 512GB model goes for CNY18,999 (~RM11,779), and the 32GB RAM + 1TB configuration is priced at CNY22,999 (~RM14,259). Meanwhile, a limited-edition bundle of the same memory and storage capacity costs CNY24,999 (~RM15,499).

Unfortunately, much like its predecessor, the MateBook Fold S may not receive an official launch in Malaysia. Huawei has yet to indicate whether it intends to bring the foldable laptop to markets outside China.

(Source: Huawei China [official website] / GSMArena)

The post You Can Now Use MyGOV Malaysia App To Renew Passports appeared first on Lowyat.NET.
item.content:encoded:
Earlier in the month, it was announced that Malaysians can apply for the 10-year passport via the Immigration Department’s MyOnline Passport service. For those who are looking to renew their passports, there’s another way to do so, which is via the MyGOV Malaysia mobile app. Bernama cites a statement by the Digital Ministry noting that this can be done once the app has been updated to version 2.1.4.

According to the report, almost the entirety of the passport renewal process can be done via the app, up until the collection of the physical passport. This means that the submission of the application and payment can be done via the MyGOV Malaysia app, with the final step being selecting the Immigration Department office where you want to collect the passport from. That being said, the selection for that last step looks to be limited, at least during the early stages.

“In the initial phase, the passport collection facility is available only at the Shaftsbury Immigration Office in Putrajaya. Other collection locations will be expanded in stages to improve access and convenience for the public nationwide”, the statement said.

Beyond the passport-related features, the report cites the ministry as saying that the app also enhances the MyNotifikasi function with more targeted, personalised notifications tailored to user needs. This lets the public receive announcements, program information, initiatives, and other important notices from ministries, departments and agencies straight from the app.

With all that said, the ministry encourages the public to download and update the MyGOV Malaysia app to the latest version via their devices’ respective app storefronts to gain access to the new features. It also says that the government “will continue to strengthen the digital services ecosystem through cross-ministry and agency cooperation to deliver more efficient, integrated and people-centric government services, in line with Malaysia’s aspiration towards an AI Nation by 2030”.

(Source: Bernama)

The post You Can Now Use MyGOV Malaysia App To Renew Passports appeared first on Lowyat.NET.

item.title: Govt Exploring Legal Amendments To Allow Digital MyKad Access Via MyGOV App
item.dc:creator: Nurul Kamil
item.description:
The MyGOV app is steadily shaping up to become the one-stop shop for various government services, with more features arriving to the platform. In the future, it may even be used to display the user’s MyKad, as the government is exploring amendments to existing laws to allow identity cards to be displayed digitally. According to […]

The post Govt Exploring Legal Amendments To Allow Digital MyKad Access Via MyGOV App appeared first on Lowyat.NET.
item.content:encoded:
The MyGOV app is steadily shaping up to become the one-stop shop for various government services, with more features arriving to the platform. In the future, it may even be used to display the user’s MyKad, as the government is exploring amendments to existing laws to allow identity cards to be displayed digitally.

According to Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo, the current legislation does not allow for the identity card to be issued in digital form. As it stands, citizens may only view their MyKad details in this way, but not display the card itself. In comparison, driving licences issued by the Road Transport Department (JPJ) can already be shown digitally, with the MyJPJ app allowing access via the user’s smartphone.

Furthermore, Gobind revealed that the government is also proposing a system that consolidates other relevant documents into a single application, and not just identity cards. These include birth certificates, marriage certificates, as well as passports. The minister went on to note that the matter had been discussed at a meeting involving GovTech, MyGOV, and MyDigital ID following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s directive to expand the digitalisation of government services.

Beyond that, Gobind also clarified that MyDigital ID will serve as a digital identity verification platform, while MyGOV will be the centralised hub for accessing multiple government apps and services. Notably, consolidating these applications into MyGOV is only the first phase. The second one will involve integrating payment systems to enable online transactions, such as for passport renewals.

Speaking of which, the MyGOV app has started rolling out the ability to renew passports. This follows a previous update that allows users to apply for identity card replacements directly through the app. However, this is limited to normal replacements without any changes, and replacements for lost or damaged cards.

(Source: Bernama)

item.title: Microsoft Declares “Code Red” After Major Outage, Targets One-Hour Recovery
item.dc:creator: Heirul Kamel
item.description:
Microsoft has reportedly declared a “Code Red” initiative to address weaknesses in its engineering infrastructure and improve its response to major service disruptions. According to Reuters, the move follows the widespread Microsoft 365 outage earlier this month, which left users around the world struggling to access Outlook, Exchange Online, Teams, Copilot, and other services. Via […]

The post Microsoft Declares “Code Red” After Major Outage, Targets One-Hour Recovery appeared first on Lowyat.NET.
item.content:encoded:
Microsoft has reportedly declared a “Code Red” initiative to address weaknesses in its engineering infrastructure and improve its response to major service disruptions. According to Reuters, the move follows the widespread Microsoft 365 outage earlier this month, which left users around the world struggling to access Outlook, Exchange Online, Teams, Copilot, and other services.

Via internal memos viewed by the publication, Microsoft considers the incident its most customer-impacting outage in the history of Exchange Online. The disruption lasted approximately 24 hours between 12 and 13 November, affecting businesses, government agencies, and other organisations across multiple countries.

As previously reported, Microsoft eventually resolved the outage after identifying a technical issue involving its network infrastructure. The company subsequently confirmed that the incident was not caused by a cyberattack or its AI agents.

Resolving Future Outages Within An Hour

The Code Red initiative is intended to address several shortcomings exposed during the incident, including how engineers coordinate their responses and manage overloaded infrastructure. According to a memo from Microsoft corporate vice president Amanda Silver, engineers exchanged more than 11,000 messages across 11 separate Teams chats while trying to resolve the outage.

However, fragmented diagnostic information and internal tracking systems made it difficult for the teams to maintain a clear picture of the situation. Silver described the experience as working through a “fog of war”, highlighting the need for better coordination during major incidents.

The initiative comprises five workstreams focusing on areas such as load shedding, geographic traffic partitioning, and faster recovery mechanisms. Microsoft also intends to deploy AI agents to help engineers analyse system health data and identify potential problems more quickly.

One of the company’s key targets is to resolve future worldwide service disruptions within an hour. This is an ambitious improvement over the recent incident, although Microsoft has not provided a timeline for when it expects to achieve this goal.

Faster Patch Deployment

Apart from outage recovery, the company is also looking to improve how quickly it deploys urgent fixes across its infrastructure. In another internal memo, Microsoft 365 Core president Jason Henderson acknowledged that some critical patches have taken too long to reach all of the company’s systems.

He cited a recent incident in which an urgent production fix took between five and six days to achieve worldwide deployment. Microsoft wants to reduce this timeframe to just one hour for its most urgent security issues, although Henderson admitted that the company is not yet close to achieving that target.

Microsoft is now placing the corrective measures under closer leadership oversight, with Henderson planning daily meetings with the Substrate leadership team and weekly reviews to track progress. The company has also reiterated its commitment to preventing similar disruptions and improving its ability to recover when problems inevitably occur.

(Source: Reuters)

The post Microsoft Declares “Code Red” After Major Outage, Targets One-Hour Recovery appeared first on Lowyat.NET.

item.dc:creator: Ian Chee
item.description:
3D printer maker Bambu Lab has announced the latest entry into its catalogue. It’s called the H3C, which is what the company dubs its first third-generation desktop 3D printer. The highlight of the product is what’s known as Swaptek, and the short version of it is that it’s the system that simplifies the usually complicated […]

The post Bambu Lab Launches H3C 3D Printer; Costs RM12,999 In Malaysia appeared first on Lowyat.NET.
item.content:encoded:
3D printer maker Bambu Lab has announced the latest entry into its catalogue. It’s called the H3C, which is what the company dubs its first third-generation desktop 3D printer. The highlight of the product is what’s known as Swaptek, and the short version of it is that it’s the system that simplifies the usually complicated process of multi-material printing into a single workflow.

Going into the nitty-gritty, the Bambu Lab H3C’s Swaptek system features a nine-tool architecture rather than just a single head. Each tool carries its own filament path and heating element, and their independence allows for material changes during the printing process to happen within six seconds. This is a massive improvement over the conventional process of having to manually switch from one filament to another.

When not in use, the nine tools are tucked away in the Retractable Rack, which also keeps their tubes from striking each other. This allows you to observe the 3D printing process in its entirety, if you choose to do so. Then there’s the FlexFeed extruder, which switches seamlessly between 1.75mm and 2.85mm filaments. Then there’s a dedicated path for TPU to keep the soft filament rigid under pressure.

Since the Bambu Lab H3C has nine independent tools as part of its system, there’s space for nine spools of filament to sit inside the AMS 3H filament tool management system’s sealed, airtight chamber. This also allows for easy colour mixing, and with just five base filaments (CMYKW), you get just about every colour you would need for your 3D prints.

The Bambu Lab H3C AMS Combo is priced in Malaysia at RM12,999. It is not available just yet, as availability starts in early December. Once that happens, you’ll be able to get it from any of the brand’s official distributors, the list of which can be found by hitting this link.
